messages.text: Beirne captains strong Ireland selection vs Fiji as Gibson-Park returns

metadata.summary: Tadhg Beirne will captain a strong Ireland selection vs Fiji in the Nations Championship on Saturday, despite head coach Andy Farrell making seven changes.
metadata.content: Nations Championship: Tadhg Beirne captains strong Ireland selection vs Fiji as Jamison Gibson-Park returns, Rob Baloucoune passed fit | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Nations Championship: Tadhg Beirne captains strong Ireland selection vs Fiji as Jamison Gibson-Park returns, Rob Baloucoune passed fit Andy Farrell's Ireland host Fiji at Aviva Stadium, Dublin on Saturday in Nations Championship (8.10pm); team selection shows seven changes to thumping win vs Argentina as Jamison Gibson-Park, Tommy O'Brien, Bundee Aki, Jamie Osborne, Ronan Kelleher, James Ryan, Josh van der Flier come in Michael Cantillon Sports Journalist Thursday 12 November 2026 14:22, UK Image: Tadhg Beirne will captain Ireland on Saturday as they host Fiji in the Nations Championship Tadhg Beirne will captain a strong Ireland selection vs Fiji in the Nations Championship on Saturday, despite head coach Andy Farrell making seven changes. Two of those changes are enforced as hooker Dan Sheehan (concussion) and No 8 Sean Jansen (knee) were ruled out, but several other injury concerns have been allayed. Indeed, wing Rob Baloucoune is fit to start again, as is Mack Hansen despite an ankle knock - the latter shifting to full-back with Hugo Keenan rested and Tommy O'Brien brought into the back-three. Josh van der Flier is also fit despite his own ankle complaint, starting at openside flanker with Nick Timoney shifting to No 8 in the absence of Jansen, Jack Conan and Caelan Doris due to injury.

messages.text: Inside Man Utd's pursuit of Pochettino

metadata.summary: Manchester United's bosses met Mauricio Pochettino two years ago, Sky Sports News can reveal, shortly after he was sacked by Chelsea, and considered him as a possible replacement for Erik ten Hag.
metadata.content: Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United: How United's pursuit of former Tottenham and Chelsea manager unfolded | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United: How United's pursuit of former Tottenham and Chelsea manager unfolded Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino set to succeed him at Old Trafford; Rob Dorsett has the full story behind the sacking and how the move for Pochettino gathered momentum and whether Unai Emery was truly ever in the running Rob Dorsett Football Correspondent @RobDorsettSky Thursday 12 November 2026 17:18, UK Manchester United's bosses met Mauricio Pochettino two years ago, Sky Sports News can reveal, shortly after he was sacked by Chelsea, and considered him as a possible replacement for Erik ten Hag. However, the decision was taken in 2024 that the timing wasn't right for either side. United are close to completing a deal for the Argentine to take over from Michael Carrick in time for the Premier League game against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday. Pochettino is a coach who has long been admired at Old Trafford. Before the INEOS takeover, he was considered for the role by the previous regime, who ultimately decided to go with Ten Hag instead. The meeting in the summer of 2024 took place shortly after Omar Berrada became United's chief executive. Ten Hag was sacked in the October. Pochettino was out of work having left Chelsea in May. metadata.content: Pierre Sage: Crystal Palace sack manager with club bottom of Premier League table after 10 matches | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Pierre Sage: Crystal Palace sack manager with club bottom of Premier League table after 10 matches Pierre Sage was appointed by Crystal Palace in the summer on a three-year contract, replacing Oliver Glasner; the former Lyon and Lens boss won just two of his 10 Premier League games in charge and the Eagles sit bottom of the table; Palace working to bring in Thomas Frank as replacement Thursday 12 November 2026 13:52, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol explains why Crystal Palace have sacked Pierre Sage and who is likely to replace him. Crystal Palace have sacked manager Pierre Sage after just 16 matches. Sage, appointed in June on a three-year contract to replace Oliver Glasner, leaves with Palace bottom of the Premier League table after winning just two of his 10 league matches in charge. Palace are working on a deal to bring in Thomas Frank as his replacement. The Dane has been out of work since he was sacked as Tottenham boss in February.
